title: A reproducible evaluation decision packet
outcome: Compute and seal a complete held-out decision packet from the connected synthetic ledger, preserving all failed and unknown conditions.

exercises.title: Change one constraint
exercises.task: Raise coverage to 0.9 while keeping the other authored inputs.
exercises.expected: Only the coverage gate passes; quality, critical cases and latency still fail.
exercises.answer: Changing one policy input cannot erase the other failures. The reference then constructs a separate all-pass input only to check the decision-rule logic; it does not invent improved observed model outcomes.

exercises.title: Keep a missing protocol result
exercises.hint: Unknown evidence cannot satisfy an explicit True requirement.
exercises.answer: A missing confirmation is reported as an unresolved condition rather than silently accepted.

exercises.title: Preserve a critical failure
exercises.expected: The critical-case gate fails even if quality improves.
exercises.hint: Required constraints are not weighted into an average.
exercises.answer: The policy gives this condition independent force; a favorable mean effect cannot cancel it.

exercises.title: Interpret zero incidents
exercises.task: Explain the positive bound for a separate hypothetical campaign with zero failures in 200 trials.
exercises.expected: Finite observations do not imply zero population risk.
exercises.hint: State the binomial and sampling assumptions.
exercises.answer: The expression 1-alpha^(1/n) assumes independent representative Bernoulli trials. It is separate from the actual authored held-out ledger, which contains one critical failure, and supplies no real-population estimate.

exercises.title: Detect an artifact edit
exercises.task: Change coverage after sealing the packet.
exercises.answer: Integrity helps reconstruct evidence but is separate from authentication and scientific validity.

exercises.title: Write a bounded memo
exercises.task: Summarize the failed packet in three sentences.
exercises.expected: State no-go, all four failing conditions and the independent evidence needed next.
exercises.answer: A useful memo identifies the decision, its supporting limits and a concrete next assessment without claiming universal quality or safety.
